title: Machine Learning Engineer
requirements: Candidates should have a degree in computer science, statistics, or a related quantitative field, along with roughly three to five years of production machine learning experience. Proficiency in Python is required, along with hands-on experience building and training models in PyTorch. Working knowledge of scikit-learn for baseline modeling and evaluation is expected, as is strong SQL for querying clinical and claims data warehouses. Prior exposure to healthcare or clinical data, including familiarity with HL7/FHIR-style records or hospital EHR exports, is preferred. Experience communicating model results to non-technical clinical stakeholders is a plus. This is a mid-level individual-contributor role reporting to the Director of Data Science.
responsibilities: You will design, train, and validate predictive models that estimate a patient's risk of hospital readmission and clinical deterioration, using structured EHR data. You will collaborate with clinical informatics staff to define target outcomes and validate model behavior against real-world discharge cases. Day to day work includes building PyTorch training pipelines, evaluating model performance with scikit-learn utilities, and writing SQL queries against the clinical data warehouse to assemble training cohorts. You will also monitor deployed models for feature drift, document modeling decisions for internal review, and periodically present findings to clinical and product stakeholders.
construction_rationale: Grade 3: ML Engineer title, full core stack (Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, SQL), healthcare domain (hospital readmission risk), and mid seniority all align exactly with Bob's profile.
